root_cause.text: On UP kernels, spin_trylock() is a no-op that always succeeds, allowing alloc_frozen_pages_nolock() called from NMI to re-enter rmqueue() and acquire a zone lock already held by the interrupted context, corrupting freelists.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "On UP kernels (!CONFIG_SMP), spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds even when the lock is already held. As a result, alloc_frozen_pages_nolock() called from NMI context can re-enter rmqueue() and acquire the zone lock that the interrupted context is already holding, corrupting the freelists." The patch adds a guard: `if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SMP) && in_nmi()) return NULL;`

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces spin_trylock() in rmqueue_bulk and rmqueue_buddy, and creates try_alloc_pages() which uses ALLOC_TRYLOCK. On UP kernels, spin_trylock always succeeds, so if these paths are entered from NMI while the zone lock is already held (e.g., from interrupted rmqueue), they will proceed to corrupt freelists. bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces spin_trylock_irqsave() in rmqueue_bulk (line 2310) and rmqueue_buddy (line 2914) with a fallback to spin_lock_irqsave only when the trylock fails and ALLOC_TRYLOCK is not set. On UP kernels, spin_trylock() is a no-op that always succeeds, so the reentrancy check (return 0/NULL when trylock fails) never triggers. This means the zone lock can be acquired again while already held if called from NMI, leading to freelist corruption. The commit does not add any UP-specific mitigation; it only bails out for PREEMPT_RT in hard IRQ/NMI, which is insufficient. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is absent.
